But the code does not do what its comment says: 'Each round picks the in-sample winner among null configurations and checks it on the same one-year holdout' - there is no in-sample data or selection; it draws independent holdout returns per round (rng.standard_normal((n_reps, rounds, n_oos))). The justification 'the in-sample choice carries no information about the holdout, so each round's holdout Sharpe ratio is a fresh draw' is a non sequitur: it gives each round the right marginal, but independence across rounds additionally requires each round's strategy to be independent of earlier rounds' strategies. Section 5 describes rounds as revisions of one idea, which are correlated (by the page's own P3, equicorrelation rho scales the inflation by sqrt(1-rho)), and an identical re-selected configuration adds nothing. The interpretation ('Five peeks ... above 1 ... twenty peeks almost 2') and Misconception 2 ('inherits the full selection bias') state the independent-rounds worst case as the general result.
rows.fix: In the code comment replace the first two sentences with 'SIMULATED null research loop. Each round tests a new configuration whose holdout returns are independent of every earlier round's; keeping the best round reports a maximum.' Put the same independence assumption in the hypothesis. Add to the interpretation: 'This assumes independent rounds; if each revision is correlated with the last, the inflation shrinks (by sqrt(1-rho) under equicorrelation, Problem P3).' In Misconception 2 replace 'inherits the full selection bias' with 'inherits the selection bias of a maximum over the rounds'.
